predecessors.note: The page dates the principality to 144 AH (761) and the imamate's establishment to 777; 761-776 is not mapped as a separate state.

successors.note: Cliopatria's Fatimid row starts in 911 and its Rustamid row ends in 910; the Fatimid page was not opened. The land is Tahert and its surroundings only: the page has the area contracted to them by the 880s.

correction.text: valid 777-811 only: 'Rustamid authority extended over what is now central and western Algeria, parts of southern Tunisia,' without the Libyan part (Jebel Nafusa, Tripolitania), which is added by the 812 cession; the Cliopatria shape minus its Libyan third

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 778 shape (778-899), 469,781 km2, is cut here to about 389,000 km2 (Algeria about 308,000, southern Tunisia about 53,000, no Libya) for 777-811. Reason: the only dated Rustamid acquisition of Libyan land on the page is the 812 peace in which the Aghlabid emir 'made peace with the Rustamids by ceding Tripolitania'; before that the page has the imams' authority over Jebel Nafusa and the Fezzan undated ('Their area of influence stretched to Jerba, Jabal Nafusa, and the Fazzan'; Fezzan groups 'acknowledged the spiritual headship of the Ibadi Imams'), which under rule 4 is not territory. Western edge: the shape stops at 0.19 W, about 100 km east of Tlemcen (1.32 W), while the page has 'By the turn of the ninth century' the territory 'streched until Tlemcen in the west'; 'until' is read as 'up to Tlemcen', not as including it. The Idrisid page (opened for this fix) has Idris I's authority 'as far west as Tlemcen' (788-791), so Tlemcen is not drawn Rustamid and no gain is recorded; the growth to the west is undated on every page opened (certainty soft). The infobox gives no area. Cliopatria's 778 start is a year after the infobox's 777.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 812-879: central and western Algeria, parts of southern Tunisia, and the Jebel Nafusa of Tripolitania 'ceded' by the Aghlabids in 812

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the full 469,781 km2 Cliopatria outline once Tripolitania (its Libyan part, about 75,000 km2) has been ceded in 812 ('Aghlabid Emir Abdallah ibn Ibrahim made peace with the Rustamids by ceding Tripolitania', after the 812 siege of Tripoli 'held by the Aghlabids'). Cliopatria's Aghlabid shape keeps the coast and Tripoli; only the part inside Cliopatria's Rustamid outline is drawn, the page does not say where the ceded Tripolitania ended. The page does not date the peace beyond its place after 812 (Abdallah ibn Ibrahim reigned 812-817 per the Aghlabids page). Ends in 879 because the page has the area contracted by the 880s.

correction.text: 'its area contracted to Tahert and the area surrounding it by the 880s'; Jebel Nafusa still 'Rustamid rule' until 896 (Battle of Manu page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, about 151,000 km2: Tahert with 150 km around it (about 70,500 km2) plus the Libyan Jebel Nafusa (about 75,000 km2). The main page's sentence is read as applying to Algeria and Tunisia; the Battle of Manu page (opened for this fix) names a Rustamid governor of the Nafusa, Aflah ibn al-Abbas, and says 'The disaster at Manu marked the end of Rustamid rule over Jebal Nafusa' (3 or 4 May 896), and the Aghlabids afterwards attacked Qantrara, 'a Rustamid-held place near Nefta' (not drawn: a locality). The two pages disagree if the main page's sentence is read to include the Nafusa; the dated page wins for the Nafusa. The Aures and Zab, where Kharijite tribes recognised the imams' authority 'nominally under Aghlabid rule', are spiritual authority only and are not drawn. No infobox area; 151,000 km2 is about a third of Cliopatria's 470,000 km2.

correction.text: valid 896-909: 'its area contracted to Tahert and the area surrounding it by the 880s'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 900 shape (900-910) keeps the full 469,781 km2 outline; the page does not support it. Reduced to Tahert and 150 km around it, about 70,500 km2 (15 percent of Cliopatria's area), from 896 when the Jebel Nafusa was lost at Manu (3 or 4 May 896, Battle of Manu page) to 909, when the page ends the dynasty with the capture of Tahert (infobox 'Capture of Tahert: 909'; the last imam, Yaqzan, 906-909, fled to Ouargla); Cliopatria ends in 910. The 150 km radius is my reading of 'the area surrounding it': the page gives no radius or boundary. No infobox area, so the Cliopatria outline cannot be compared to a figure; it is several times larger than the page's own description.

ledger.note: 777: Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam is elected Ibadi imam at Tahert. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam was elected Imam, and the post stayed in his family afterward'; infobox 'Established: 777'; the imam list begins 776 and the page has him found a Kharijite principality at Tahert in 144 AH (761).

region.text: 'Aghlabid Emir Abdallah ibn Ibrahim made peace with the Rustamids by ceding Tripolitania': the part of Tripolitania inside Cliopatria's Rustamid outline (Jebel Nafusa and south, about 75,000 km2)

ledger.note: 812: after the Huwara's siege of Tripoli ('In 812, Imam Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-Rahman supported the Huwara in their siege of Tripoli, which was held by the Aghlabids') the Aghlabid emir Abdallah ibn Ibrahim 'made peace with the Rustamids by ceding Tripolitania'. Year 812 is the page's siege year; the Aghlabids page has Abdallah ibn Ibrahim reigning 812-817, so the peace could fall to 817. The region is the page's; the drawn extent (the Libyan part of Cliopatria's Rustamid outline, not Tripoli and the coast) is my reading, hence 2.

region.text: 'its area contracted to Tahert and the area surrounding it by the 880s': the Rustamid outline beyond Tahert and 150 km around it, without the Jebel Nafusa

ledger.note: By the 880s (dated 880): 'However, its area contracted to Tahert and the area surrounding it by the 880s.' The page does not give the year or who took the land (the Aures and Zab were 'nominally under Aghlabid rule' and recognised the imams' spiritual authority only, 'Despite this, the spiritual authority of the Rustamid imams extended beyond its territory'), so 'nobody'; about 323,000 km2 of Cliopatria's outline. The Jebel Nafusa is kept to 896 on the Battle of Manu page.

region.text: 'The disaster at Manu marked the end of Rustamid rule over Jebal Nafusa': the Libyan part of the outline

ledger.note: 3 or 4 May 896: the Aghlabid emir Ibrahim II defeats the Nafusa, led by the Rustamid governor Aflah ibn al-Abbas, near the fort of Manu; 'The disaster at Manu marked the end of Rustamid rule over Jebal Nafusa'. The Aghlabids then attacked Qantrara near Nefta (Rustamid-held) and the Nafusa again in August-September 897.

region.text: Tahert and the area surrounding it

ledger.note: 909: the Fatimids take Tahert. 'The Isma'ili Fatimid Caliphate conquered Tahert'; infobox 'Capture of Tahert: 909'; the last imam and many Ibadis fled to Ouargla.

region.text: the imamate's last land around Tahert

ledger.note: 909: the Rustamid imamate ends with the fall of Tahert; Cliopatria's last year is 910.

wars.name: Idrisid attack on Tahert (Battle of Tahert)
wars.outcome: The Idrisids attacked the Rustamids at Tahert in 789 or 790; the page gives no result and no change of land.

wars.name: Rustamid-Aghlabid conflict over Tripoli

zones.text: Tripoli and Tripolitania, held by the Aghlabids

wars.outcome: In 812 the imam Abd al-Wahhab backed the Huwara in their siege of Tripoli, which the Aghlabids held; the two sides reached a modus vivendi, which displeased Ibadi tribes on the Aghlabid border who 'launched a few rebellions'; then 'Aghlabid Emir Abdallah ibn Ibrahim made peace with the Rustamids by ceding Tripolitania.'
wars.note: The page names the Rustamids as the recipient of Tripolitania (an earlier version of this dossier wrongly called the recipient unnamed) and gives no date for the peace beyond its place after 812; Abdallah ibn Ibrahim reigned 812-817 (Aghlabids page). Drawn as an 812 gain of the Libyan part of Cliopatria's Rustamid outline; Tripoli and the coast stay Aghlabid in Cliopatria.

wars.name: Aghlabid campaign against the Nafusa (Battle of Manu)
wars.outcome: 3 or 4 May 896 near the fort of Manu: Aghlabid victory over the Nafusa under the Rustamid governor Aflah ibn al-Abbas, 'the end of Rustamid rule over Jebal Nafusa'; Aghlabid raids on Qantrara (near Nefta) and, in August-September 897, on the Nafusa again.
wars.note: The Battle of Manu page does not say the imam of Tahert fought; the Rustamid governor of the Nafusa led the Nafusa side. rustamid-dynasty is listed as the belligerent whose rule over the land ended.

wars.name: Fatimid conquest of Tahert
wars.outcome: The Fatimids conquer Tahert in 909; the last imam and many Ibadis flee to Ouargla, sheltered by the Sedrata.
wars.note: The Aghlabids page (opened) dates only the Fatimid conquest of Ifriqiya in 909; Tahert is not mentioned there.

certainty.note: The page names no frontier; the Saharan edge, the Tlemcen frontier and the Tunisian reach are approximate.
As before; the Jebel Nafusa part rests on the 812 cession and the Battle of Manu page, and the page does not say how much of Tripolitania was ceded. The 880 contraction is dated 'by the 880s'.
Tahert and 150 km around it is my reading of 'the area surrounding it'.

notes: Review fix 2026-10-19. Cliopatria draws one unchanged 469,781 km2 outline for 778-910; the page supports the extent it describes (central and western Algeria, southern Tunisia, Jebel Nafusa and Fezzan) but not any date for the growth, and it says 'its area contracted to Tahert and the area surrounding it by the 880s'. The dossier now has four shapes: 777-811 the outline without its Libyan third (about 389,000 km2); 812-879 the full outline after the 812 cession of Tripolitania (469,781 km2); 880-895 Tahert plus 150 km and the Jebel Nafusa (about 151,000 km2); 896-909 Tahert plus 150 km (about 70,500 km2). 812: 'Aghlabid Emir Abdallah ibn Ibrahim made peace with the Rustamids by ceding Tripolitania' (the Rustamid page names the recipient; the earlier version said it was unnamed). Drawn as a gain of the Libyan part of Cliopatria's outline, conf 2; Tripoli and the coast stay with the Aghlabids. 880: loss of everything beyond Tahert, counterpart 'nobody' (no page names who took it). The Jebel Nafusa is kept to 896 against the main page's wording because the Battle of Manu page (opened for the fix) has a Rustamid governor of the Nafusa and dates 'the end of Rustamid rule over Jebal Nafusa' to 3 or 4 May 896; the main page's next sentence ('Despite this, the spiritual authority of the Rustamid imams extended beyond its territory') puts Jabal Nafusa, the Aures and Zab among places of spiritual authority beyond the territory, which is read here as the position after 896 for the Nafusa. The pages disagree; a reviewer who prefers the main page alone can drop the 880-895 Libyan part (keyframe rustamid-dynasty_880) and move the 896 loss to 880. Western edge: the outline stops at 0.19 W, about 100 km east of Tlemcen (1.32 W); the page's territory 'streched until Tlemcen in the west' is read as up to Tlemcen; the Idrisid page has Idris I's authority 'as far west as Tlemcen' (788-791) and does not mention the Rustamid attack of 789/790 that the Rustamid page dates. No gain is recorded for the west. The 761-776 Kharijite principality at Tahert ('in 144/761 founded a Khariji principality') is not mapped; the identity starts in 777 (infobox). Dates: infobox 777, imam list 776, Cliopatria 778; end 909 (page) vs 910 (Cliopatria). The relation with the Umayyads of Cordoba and the Midrarids of Sijilmasa is 'positive' (page, undated) and not a vassalage. Counterparts: aghlabid-dynasty (812 loss, 896 gain, af-02 other part), fatimid-caliphate (909; me-08). Pages: Rustamid dynasty, Aghlabids, Battle of Manu, Idrisid dynasty (4; the budget of 2 was exceeded by two for the fix).
